tagline: Old US 7, between the Taconics and the Green Mountains.
intro: The road comes up from the Massachusetts line at Pownal on US 7, and at Bennington it turns off onto the old highway, signed Historic 7A. From there it keeps to the valley between the Taconic Range and the Green Mountains, through South Shaftsbury and Arlington, where the Batten Kill swings west for New York, and on to Manchester.

Bennington is the South Shire and Manchester the North Shire, and the old highway joins the two. Arlington, along the way, was the first capital of the Vermont Republic in 1777, and the Batten Kill running through it is known for its trout.

moments.title: Old Bennington
moments.text: On a hill above downtown, the Old First Church of 1806 shares the village with a 306-foot stone obelisk raised for a battle that was actually fought over the line in New York.

moments.title: Robert Frost Stone House
moments.text: Frost bought this 1769 stone farmhouse in 1920 to farm apples, wrote "Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening" in it, and the orchard has since been replanted from one of his last trees.

moments.title: Hildene
moments.text: Robert Todd Lincoln's summer house of 1905 stands on a promontory over the Battenkill Valley, beside a garden laid out in privet in the pattern of a stained-glass window.
